title: Galuh Kingdom
capsule: The Kingdom of Galuh was a Sundanese Hindu-Buddhist polity in what is now West and Central Java, Indonesia, emerging in the seventh century as an eastern breakaway from the declining Tarumanagara kingdom with its heartland between the Citarum and Cipamali rivers. Galuh maintained a rival and intermittently unified relationship with the Sunda Kingdom to its west, with periods of merger under a single crown and periods of independent rule from capitals including Karangkamulyan and Kawali. The kingdom's court culture produced the Carita Parahyangan, an important Old Sundanese chronicle, and its rulers legitimized authority through both Indic and indigenous Sunda Wiwitan religious frameworks. By the fifteenth century Galuh was absorbed into the unified Sunda polity centered on Pakuan Pajajaran, which itself fell to Banten and Cirebon by 1579.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial limits of Galuh are reconstructed from inscriptions, the Carita Parahyangan chronicle, and later Sundanese texts; boundaries are approximate and scholarly consensus on the kingdom's phases remains incomplete.
